key_insight: The paper uses reinforcement learning to make relay-side bundle scheduling and dropping decisions in deep-space networks more goal-aware, fairness-aware, and contact-feasible.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical control framework for managing scarce storage and intermittent links in delay-tolerant space communications, where standard FIFO scheduling can waste valuable contact opportunities.
method: Models relay control as a constrained semi-Markov decision process (CSMDP).
Uses masked Lagrangian PPO to learn scheduling, dropping, and flow-control policies.
Applies feasibility-aware action masking so only bundles that can finish within the remaining contact window are transmitted.
evidence_signal: DTNSim simulations show improved age-based utility and inter-flow fairness compared with baseline schedulers.
watch_item: Performance depends on simulation fidelity and on how well the learned policy transfers to real deep-space contact patterns and mission-specific utility functions.
paper_title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
